{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1961)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}}
[[File:Ursula Hamenstädt, circa 1986 (re-scanned, headshot).jpg|thumb|right|240px|Ursula Hamenstädt, Berkeley 1986]]
'''Ursula Hamenstädt''' (born 15 January 1961) is a German mathematician who works as a professor at the [[University of Bonn]].<ref name="profile">[http://www.hcm.uni-bonn.de/people/profile/ursula-hamenstaedt/ Faculty profile], [[University of Bonn]], retrieved 18 December 2014.</ref> Her primary research subject is [[differential geometry]].

== Education and career ==
Hamenstädt earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 1986, under the supervision of [[Wilhelm Klingenberg]].
Her dissertation, ''Zur Theorie der Carnot-Caratheodory Metriken und ihren Anwendungen'' [''The theory of Carnot–Caratheodory metrics and their applications''], concerned the theory of [[sub-Riemannian manifold]]s.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=23543}}</ref>

After completing her doctorate, she became a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Research Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and then an assistant professor at the [[California Institute of Technology]] before returning to Bonn as a faculty member in 1990.<ref name="profile"/>

== Honors ==
Hamenstädt was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Hamenstädt
 | first = Ursula
 | contribution = Actions of the mapping class group
 | mr = 2827829
 | pages = 1002–1021
 | publisher = Hindustan Book Agency
 | location = New Delhi
 | title = Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians. Volume II
 | url = http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2010.2/Main/icm2010.2.1002.1021.pdf
 | year = 2010
 | access-date = 19 December 2014
 | archive-date = 19 December 2014
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141219043126/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2010.2/Main/icm2010.2.1002.1021.pdf
 | url-status = dead
 }}.</ref> In 2012 she was elected to the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]],<ref>[http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/7550/ List of members: Prof. Dr. Ursula Hamenstädt], Leopoldina, retrieved 18 December 2014.</ref> and in the same year she became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=25 August 2018 }}, retrieved 18 December 2014.</ref>
She was the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2017.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv/preise-auszeichnungen|title=Preise und Auszeichnungen|publisher=[[German Mathematical Society]]|language=German|access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>
